pairs.difference: A: the umbrella's top rim is dark and firm, while the under-canopy panels fade to thin lost edges, and the pole is crisp. B: the star's contour is heavy on the upper-left arms and drops out on the lit lower bevels; the rivet balls have closed dark rings. Both have clean outer edges with no halo, sparse interiors and faint background rings, as on the real cards. A's subject density (0.042) is only just under the real range, which fits its large plain canopy.

A: the boot carries dashed stitch rows, inlaid flame shapes, a spur and leather grain, and the argyle background is a hard, full-card net of lines. Subject density (0.184) and background density (0.039) are both above the real range, and background and hero compete at similar sharpness. B: the cap has a few long clean contours, soft concentric rings and a plain interior, within range and like the real cards.
pairs.fix: Make the background a soft, low-contrast pattern with blurred divisions, with no sharp diamond lines. Reduce the boot to a few large shapes, removing the dashed stitching and fine leather grain. Keep the sharpest edges only on the toe, spur and top of the shaft.

pairs.difference: A: the jacket is broken up by pocket flaps, collar seams, sash borders and closed dark rings around each badge, with an even contour across the whole form and dense background rays. Subject density (0.159) sits just above the real range. B: the hat has one long contour that thins on the lit crown, a single band line and an almost empty interior, with lost edges like the real cards.
pairs.fix: Simplify the jacket to fewer seams and soft, shallow pocket folds. Let the outer edge fade where light hits the shoulder and sleeves. Keep crisp edges only around the badges, with no dark ring around each one.

pairs.difference: B: the sign boards have soft, smeared edges with blotchy black pooling under the arrows, a wobbly embossed look around the plank seams and fuzzy clouds with sharp ink-like tails. Subject density (0.083) is below the real range. A: the booth's edges are straight and precise, with thin even glazing bars and clean suitcase motifs behind. It is a little mechanical but stays crisp at the hero and quieter in the background.
pairs.fix: Give the wooden boards clean, firm silhouettes with thin, straight plank gaps. Remove the dark smudges under the arrows. Make the clouds soft-edged, with no sharp dark tails.

pairs.difference: B: the string grid is a dense black mesh, the court lines are razor-sharp black rules running edge to edge and the grip has hard segments. All three measures are outside the real range (subject 0.281, background 0.037 is the exception at the high end, outline -0.167). A: the cactus is underdense (0.063) with soft ribs, but it has lost edges and a calm silhouette. Its one flaw is grainy noise in the sand. The racket's strings explain part of B's density, so this is not certain.
pairs.fix: Draw the strings as a soft, simplified grid with fewer, lighter lines. Blur the court lines slightly so they are softer than the racket. Give the racket a firm rim that softens on its lit side.

pairs.difference: A: the suitcase has a dark contour with a doubled edge around the body and corners, and each sticker has a heavy closed double ring. Outline darkness (0.128) is above the real range and reads as a drawn contour. Rust flecks add small scattered edges. B: the barrel's stave gaps are dark and thick, but the outer edge is plain and the hoops are almost edgeless. Its values are within the real range.
pairs.fix: Remove the dark line around the suitcase and let its edge come only from the color change against the background. Make the sticker borders thin and clean with no double contour. Drop the small rust scratches.

pairs.difference: A: the rock surface is a field of gritty micro-edges and the speckles scatter hundreds of tiny dots across the pot, so the card has noise edges that no real card shows. Background density (0.023) is slightly above range. B: the sneakers have thin, precise panel seams and a mesh patch, with a single horizon rule. Subject density is at the top of the range (0.227) and outline darkness (-0.100) is below it, so the call is not one-sided.
pairs.fix: Replace the gritty rock with a smooth stone surface with a few broad soft cracks. Replace the many tiny speckles with a handful of larger soft dots. Keep the sharpest edges at the rim, lid and spout.

pairs.difference: B: the poster has a heavy, wobbly dark contour, torn corners and many crease lines, and the plank background is dense with sharp grain and knots. Background density (0.059) is above the real range and the background competes with the hero. A: the locker has clean, thin door gaps, simple vents and a quiet background with only a soft skirting line. Its outline value is marginally low but the map looks like the real cards.
pairs.fix: Make the wooden wall soft and low detail, with a few faint plank gaps and no grain or knots. Give the poster a clean edge with fewer tears and creases, and no dark line around it.

pairs.difference: A: the saloon has continuous dark lines around every plank, baluster and window, at the same weight from foreground steps to the distant buildings, like inked linework with no edge hierarchy. B: the dock's edges vary more. The rope is dense, but the post tops, water and sand fall away to soft or lost edges. Numbers for both are within range, so this rests on the eye and the object types differ.
pairs.fix: Remove the dark line weight from the building. Keep crisp edges on the doorway and balcony, soften plank lines toward the sides and blur the far buildings so they have almost no lines.

pairs.difference: A: the wagon has a strong canvas contour and fine grass strokes, but the far hills and clouds soften. B: the dock has thick dark plank gaps and many sharp water ripples, but the boat's lit rim stays clean. Each has one flaw, the values for both are within range, and neither gives a clear reason to choose.

B: the ivy fills the frame with hundreds of closed leaf contours, the wreath is as dense as its surroundings, and the door has grain lines and smeared shadow edges around the wreath and handle. Subject density (0.342) and background density (0.107) are both above the real range, with no resting area for the eye. A: the windmill is detailed but has a clear hierarchy, with crisp blades and tower and faint clouds and mesas behind.
pairs.fix: Replace the many small ivy leaves with a few large, soft leaf clusters at the corners. Make the door plain and smooth with no wood grain. Keep the sharpest edges on the wreath only.

pairs.difference: A: the bumper car has a firm contour that softens across the green shell, with a few clean floor lines and blurred reflections. B: the fins have a crisp rim with a double line along the blade edges and a very quiet ring background. Background density of 0.005 is just below range, but this comes from the plain background rather than an edge flaw. Neither shows a drawn outline or a halo.

pattern: Generated cards are given away by edges spread evenly instead of placed by importance. Small detail such as stitching, grain, speckle, leaves and creases is sharp everywhere, and backgrounds are as crisp as the hero. Contours stay closed and even around every shape, often doubled around sub-parts, where real cards let them thin or vanish on lit sides and use few internal lines with quiet backgrounds. Lens maps at this scale can also reflect subject type, so density alone is weak evidence on detail-heavy objects.
